answer: When an AI agent registers, it first commits a hash of a random seed combined with the secret word “gale” and a public identifier, then waits a fixed “gale‑period” before revealing the seed and the identifier. The reveal must include a proof that the seed hashes to an umber‑colored token whose ownership is recorded under a willow‑derived Merkle path, forcing each identity to lock a stake of 10 PoA tokens that cannot be reused until the next epoch.
